findings.title: Lack of Documented Review of Required Quarterly Reports (federal, AL 97.036 FEMA Public Assistance)
findings.plain: 3 of 40 quarterly FEMA (Hurricane Michael) reports prepared by the county's consultant did not match approved expenses and support. There was no documented county review before the consultant submitted them. Material weakness; no questioned costs.
findings.mgmt_response: Will add a formal, signed review of quarterly FEMA reports before submission.

findings.title: Ineligible Expenses Approved for Reimbursement (federal, AL 97.083 SAFER fire staffing grant)
findings.plain: Two of three reimbursement requests tested included ineligible payroll costs approved by the grant administrator. The federal grantor caught them and paid only eligible costs. Material weakness; no questioned costs.
findings.mgmt_response: Additional review, including by the Clerk of Court Board Finance Office, documented by email approval.

findings.title: Material audit adjustments (Bay County financial statements)
findings.plain: Material adjustments were needed for the financial statements to meet GAAP because county controls did not catch them in time. Material weakness.
findings.mgmt_response: Finance Office will identify and record proposed adjustments more timely, coordinating with departments. Target 10/1/2025.

findings.title: Material adjustments - Bay County Property Appraiser
findings.plain: The Property Appraiser's office needed material adjustments to cash and accounts payable, and a check was improperly dated in its records. Material weakness.

audits.financial_condition_notes: County did not meet any s. 218.503(1) condition; no management letter recommendations for the Board or the constitutional officers; prior-year findings reported corrected (including the permit-fee finding).

audits.opinion: Unmodified; federal and state compliance unmodified.

findings.title: Permit fees not charged per adopted fee schedule (first reported 2020)
findings.plain: Because of problems in the permit system, the county charged some permit fees that did not match the fee schedule set by Resolutions 3945 and 3957, overcharging in some cases; the county booked a payable for the estimated excess. Auditor recommended fixing the system and remedying affected permits.
findings.mgmt_response: Corrective action plan attached to report; reported corrected in FY2024.

findings.title: Material adjustments - Bay County Sheriff
findings.plain: The Sheriff's office needed material adjustments to cash, expenses, unearned revenue, payables and accrued liabilities. Material weakness.

findings.title: Audit Adjusting Entries (first reported 2024)
findings.plain: Significant corrections were needed, including unearned state funds not identified, an unrecorded IT subscription agreement, misclassified capital spending, and OPEB, accrual and lease adjustments. The auditor ties it partly to a lack of appropriate staffing.
findings.mgmt_response: Not corrected; per district, still having significant staff turnover and understaffing.

findings.title: Expenditures not limited to budgeted amounts (first reported by Auditor General as AM 2023-001)
findings.plain: General Fund spending exceeded the budget in three functional categories by a total of $326,700, and the Board did not amend the budget by September 10 as state law and Board policy require. Caused by year-end adjustments not reflected in budget monitoring.
findings.mgmt_response: Over-expenditures came from year-end reclassifications and accruals; still implementing a detailed year-end budget-to-actual review.

findings.title: Return of Title IV funds worksheets not documented as independently reviewed (federal, Pell Grant, Haney Technical College)
findings.plain: Refunds of federal student aid were calculated correctly, but there was no sign-off showing an independent review. Material weakness; no questioned costs.
findings.mgmt_response: Corrective action plan attached to report.

findings.title: Return of Title IV funds not made within required timeline (federal, Pell Grant)
findings.plain: For 2 of 9 students tested, federal aid was returned to the U.S. Department of Education after the 45-day deadline because of manual-control human error. Could risk future Pell funding. Significant deficiency.
findings.mgmt_response: Corrective action plan attached to report.

findings.title: Multi-factor authentication not required for student information (federal, Pell / Gramm-Leach-Bliley)
findings.plain: The district's system did not require multi-factor authentication to access student information, as federal student-information security rules require. Material weakness.
findings.mgmt_response: Corrective action plan attached to report.

findings.plain: Heavy turnover: from Jan. 2020 to Aug. 2024 the City Administrator position turned over 3 times, City Clerk 2 times, and City Accountant 3 times (vacant 495 days). Records showed allegations of a negative workplace and conflicts between management and elected officials.

Audits and annual financial reports were filed late for FY2020-21 through FY2022-23 (FY2021-22 audit was 362 days late). The Department of Revenue withheld $37,137 ($29,166 half-cent sales tax + $7,971 municipal revenue sharing) as of August 2024.

Competitive procurement not followed: 5 purchases totaling $564,092 (including $250,000 disaster debris removal, $130,772 fuel from the same local vendor for at least 19 years, $110,260 yard waste) were not competitively selected; other bids/RFPs lacked advertising documentation.
9 purchases totaling $1 million lacked City Council approval required for purchases over $10,000; purchase orders were not used as required, and receipt of goods/services was not always documented.
The city paid a contractor the same $450,031 invoice twice; the contractor refunded $328,964 on Dec. 13, 2023 (the duplicate less $121,067 retainage).
The city kept paying its contracted City Accountant after the agreement expired (April 2021) and issued 1099s instead of W-2s without documenting why she was treated as an independent contractor.
Application security: user access privileges were not limited to what was necessary.
IT access was not always promptly removed when no longer needed.
No policies for reporting, investigating and communicating known or suspected fraud.

Controls over construction management entity (CME) subcontractor services and payments still needed improvement.

state_reports.type: Federal indictment (charges, not a finding of guilt)

findings.plain: A 64-count indictment charged Mayor Margo Anderson and City Attorney Joseph Adam Albritton with conspiracy, wire fraud, honest services fraud and theft concerning federal programs tied to Hurricane Michael cleanup. It alleged $1.8 million billed to the city for unnecessary trash pickup by contractor ECS, over $48,000 of unauthorized cleanup work at Anderson-related residences, $25,000 at Albritton-related residences, and a $106,000 motorhome given to Anderson and her husband. These are allegations; case outcomes were not confirmed from an official DOJ or court source in this research.

Total debt means bonds, notes, loans, leases, subscription IT arrangements (SBITAs) and finance purchases (plus unamortized bond premium where reported). It excludes compensated absences, claims, landfill closure costs, net pension and OPEB liabilities, which are shown separately.

Latest audit used: FY2025 for Lynn Haven, Callaway, Springfield, Parker, Mexico Beach, Panama City Beach, PCB CRA and the airport district; FY2025 (June 30) for Bay District Schools; FY2024 for Bay County, Panama City, Panama City CRA and the Port Authority, because their FY2025 audits were not on the Auditor General's site as of 2026-10-20.

Almost all local debt here is privately placed with banks or borrowed from the State (State Revolving Fund, State Infrastructure Bank), not publicly sold bonds, so most issues have no credit rating or EMMA listing.

Big near-term balloon payments: Panama City's $150,000,000 Series 2023 note (5.82%) is scheduled to be repaid in one payment in FY2026. Bay County's Hurricane Michael notes are due in one payment each: $49,943,109 on 9/1/2027 and $48,874,337 on 9/1/2028.
Debt service 'year' is the first scheduled year in each audit's maturity table (the year after the audit), unless otherwise noted.

No government reviewed met any s. 218.503(1) financial emergency condition in the audits reviewed. No auditor issued a deteriorating-financial-condition notice. Mexico Beach's FY2022 audit noted late vendor payments tied to Hurricane Michael grant timing, which the auditor said was not a financial emergency.
Only Mexico Beach received a modified (qualified) opinion. The cause, in FY2023-FY2025, was that the city had not implemented GASB 75 (retiree health/OPEB).
gaps: Bay County, City of Panama City, Panama City CRA and Panama City Port Authority FY2025 audits were not filed on the Auditor General site as of 2026-10-20, so FY2024 is used. The Port Authority has only its FY2024 audit posted there.

Credit ratings: none of the audits publish ratings, and Moody's/S&P pages could not be read. The only publicly offered bonds found are Bay County's Water & Sewer 2015 and Water 2016 bonds, Callaway 2015, Lynn Haven 2015/2016, and probably the school COPs. Their ratings still need to be checked in the official statements.
EMMA (emma.msrb.org), the national bond disclosure site, couldn't be read by our tools, so bond documents there are not linked yet.

Original issue amounts are missing for several issues (Mexico Beach, Lynn Haven bonds, Port loans), and per-series COP balances are missing for the school district, because the audits do not list them.

Purposes are not stated in the audits for Panama City's $150M Series 2023 note (beyond 'Capital Projects Fund'), the airport's SIB loans, and most Port loans. Council and board minutes or loan resolutions would be needed.

Management responses: several reports attach corrective action plans as scanned images (Panama City CRA, PCB 2024, Bay DSB 2025, some Bay County items). Where the text couldn't be read, the page says so.

CRAs for Callaway, Springfield and Parker file separate reports. They were not reviewed because the city audits show no CRA debt. Springfield's and Parker's own audits report late or missing city TIF payments to those CRAs.
Lynn Haven federal corruption case: only the 2020 DOJ indictment release was confirmed. Plea and sentencing outcomes need official DOJ or court documents.

FY2022 audits were reviewed only where needed to complete 3 years (Panama City, Panama City CRA, Bay County). Prior-year findings for the other governments are summarized from the later audits' prior-finding schedules, with brief plain-English text.
